questions.summary: Differentiate a linear-plus-sine function and determine its tangent at x = π.
questions.accessibleText:
1. [Maximum mark: 6]

Consider the function f(x) = 2x + sin x, x ∈ ℝ.

(a) Find f′(x). [2]

(b) Hence, find the equation of the tangent to the graph of f at the point where x = π. [4]
questions.solution: (a) For f(x)=2x+sin x, f′(x)=2+cos x. (b) f(π)=2π and f′(π)=2+cos π=1. The tangent through (π,2π) is y−2π=x−π, so y=x+π.
questions.solutionStatus: Independent worked solution — not an official IB markscheme

questions.summary: Use the symmetry of a factored quadratic to find an unknown root, its vertex, and its range.
questions.accessibleText:
2. [Maximum mark: 5]

Consider the function f(x) = 3(x − 2)(x − q), where x ∈ ℝ and q is a real constant.

The axis of symmetry of the graph of f has equation x = 4.

(a) Show that q = 6. [2]

(b) Find the coordinates of the vertex of the graph of f. [2]

(c) Hence, write down the range of f. [1]
questions.solution: The roots of f(x)=3(x−2)(x−q) are 2 and q. (a) Their midpoint is the symmetry axis, so (2+q)/2=4 and q=6. (b) At x=4, f(4)=3(2)(−2)=−12, hence the vertex is (4,−12). (c) The leading coefficient is positive, so the range is f(x)≥−12.
questions.solutionStatus: Independent worked solution — not an official IB markscheme

questions.summary: Integrate a given velocity and use the initial position to obtain displacement.
questions.accessibleText:
3. [Maximum mark: 5]

A particle P is travelling along a straight line, with displacement measured relative to a point O on the line. The velocity, v m s⁻¹, of the particle at time t seconds is given by

v = 1/(t + 1) + e⁻ᵗ, where t ≥ 0.

(a) Find ∫(1/(t + 1) + e⁻ᵗ) dt. [2]

Initially the particle is at O.

(b) Find an expression for the displacement, s metres, in terms of t. [3]
questions.solution: (a) ∫(1/(t+1)+e^(−t))dt=ln|t+1|−e^(−t)+C. (b) Since t≥0, s(t)=ln(t+1)−e^(−t)+C. Initially s(0)=0, so 0=0−1+C and C=1. Thus s(t)=ln(t+1)−e^(−t)+1 metres.
questions.solutionStatus: Independent worked solution — not an official IB markscheme

questions.summary: Recover the positive common ratio and an earlier term of a geometric sequence from two later terms.
questions.accessibleText:
4. [Maximum mark: 6]

Consider a geometric sequence, uₙ, with common ratio r, where each term in the sequence is positive.

It is given that u₆ = 1.6 × 10⁵ and u₈ = 6.4 × 10⁵.

(a) Find the value of r. [3]

(b) Find the value of u₁, giving your answer in the form a × 10ᵏ, where 1 ≤ a < 10 and k ∈ ℤ. [3]
questions.solution: Because u8=u6r², r²=(6.4×10^5)/(1.6×10^5)=4. Every term is positive, so r=2. Also u6=u1r^5, hence u1=(1.6×10^5)/2^5=5000=5×10^3, which has the required scientific-notation form.
questions.solutionStatus: Independent worked solution — not an official IB markscheme

questions.summary: Rewrite a base-25 logarithm using base 5, then solve a logarithmic equation involving a cube root.
questions.accessibleText:
5. [Maximum mark: 7]

(a) Show that log₂₅(81x²) = log₅9 + log₅x for x > 0. [4]

(b) Hence, solve the equation log₅∛x = log₂₅(81x²) − log₅4, where x > 0. [3]
questions.solution: (a) For x>0, log_25(81x²)=log_5(81x²)/log_5 25=(log_5 81+2log_5 x)/2=log_5 9+log_5 x. (b) Using this identity, log_5(x^(1/3))=log_5(9x)−log_5 4=log_5(9x/4). Thus x^(1/3)=9x/4. Dividing by x^(1/3)>0 gives x^(2/3)=4/9, so x=(2/3)^3=8/27.
questions.solutionStatus: Independent worked solution — not an official IB markscheme

questions.summary: Combine probabilities from a Venn diagram and impose independence to determine a parameter.
questions.accessibleText:
6. [Maximum mark: 9]

Consider two events, A and B.

It is given that P(A ∩ B′) = (5 + x)/24, P(A ∩ B) = (7 − x)/12 and P(A′ ∩ B) = 1/6, where 0 ≤ x ≤ 7.

(a) Show that P(A) = (19 − x)/24. [3]

It is given that A and B are independent.

(b) Find the possible values of x. [6]
questions.solution: (a) P(A)=P(A∩B′)+P(A∩B)=(5+x)/24+(7−x)/12=(5+x+14−2x)/24=(19−x)/24. (b) P(B)=P(A′∩B)+P(A∩B)=1/6+(7−x)/12=(9−x)/12. Independence requires (7−x)/12=[(19−x)/24][(9−x)/12]. Hence 24(7−x)=(19−x)(9−x), which simplifies to x²−4x+3=0. Therefore x=1 or x=3; both satisfy 0≤x≤7.
questions.solutionStatus: Independent worked solution — not an official IB markscheme

questions.summary: Analyze a rational-function graph, including asymptotes, intercepts, a vertical translation, and the resulting range.
questions.accessibleText:
7. [Maximum mark: 12]

Consider the function f(x) = (2x − 3)/(3 − x), x ∈ ℝ, x ≠ 3.

The graph of f and its asymptotes are shown in the following diagram.

[Diagram: Coordinate axes labelled x and y with origin O. The graph y = f(x) has two hyperbola-like branches separated by a dashed vertical asymptote to the right of the y-axis. A dashed horizontal asymptote lies below the x-axis. The left branch crosses both coordinate axes, approaches the horizontal asymptote from above as x decreases, and rises without bound as it approaches the vertical asymptote from the left. The right branch lies below the horizontal asymptote, falls without bound near the vertical asymptote, and approaches the horizontal asymptote from below as x increases.]

(a) Find the equation of
    (i) the vertical asymptote;
    (ii) the horizontal asymptote. [3]

(b) Find the coordinates of the points where the graph of f intersects the coordinate axes. [4]

Consider the function g(x) = x + 4, x ∈ ℝ.

(c) (i) Describe the transformation that transforms the graph of y = f(x) to the graph of y = (g ∘ f)(x).
    (ii) Hence, find the range of g ∘ f. [5]
questions.solution: For f(x)=(2x−3)/(3−x): (a)(i) The denominator vanishes at x=3, so the vertical asymptote is x=3. (a)(ii) The ratio of leading coefficients is 2/(−1)=−2, so the horizontal asymptote is y=−2. (b) Setting the numerator to zero gives the x-intercept (3/2,0); f(0)=−1 gives the y-intercept (0,−1). (c)(i) Since g(x)=x+4, (g∘f)(x)=f(x)+4, a translation by vector (0,4). (c)(ii) The range of f excludes −2, so the translated range excludes 2: range(g∘f)=ℝ\{2}.
questions.solutionStatus: Independent worked solution — not an official IB markscheme

questions.summary: Determine coefficients and stationary-point behavior of a cubic from an inflection point and horizontal tangents.
questions.accessibleText:
8. [Maximum mark: 15]

Consider the function f(x) = ax³ + bx² + cx + d, where x ∈ ℝ and where a, b, c and d are real constants.

The graph of f has a point of inflexion at (−2, −2c + d + 24).

(a) Show that a = 3/2 and b = 9. [6]

It is given that the tangents to the graph of f at x = −3 and x = k are horizontal.

(b) (i) Show that c = 27/2.
    (ii) Find the value of k.
    (iii) State whether f has a local maximum or a local minimum at x = k, justifying your answer. [7]

The graph of f intersects the y-axis at the point P.

(c) Show that the tangent to the graph of f at x = −3 passes through P. [2]
questions.solution: Let f(x)=ax³+bx²+cx+d. Then f′(x)=3ax²+2bx+c and f″(x)=6ax+2b. (a) The inflection at x=−2 gives −12a+2b=0, so b=6a. Also f(−2)=−2c+d+24 gives −8a+4b=24, or −2a+b=6. Therefore a=3/2 and b=9. (b)(i) Horizontal tangent at x=−3 means f′(−3)=0: (9/2)(9)+18(−3)+c=0, so c=27/2. (ii) Now f′(x)=(9/2)(x²+4x+3)=(9/2)(x+1)(x+3). Besides −3, the stationary point is k=−1. (iii) At −1, f′ changes from negative to positive (equivalently f″(−1)=9>0), so f has a local minimum. (c) P=(0,d). Substituting x=−3 into f gives f(−3)=−81/2+81−81/2+d=d. Since f′(−3)=0, the tangent there is y=d, which passes through P.
questions.solutionStatus: Independent worked solution — not an official IB markscheme

questions.summary: Determine constants in a trigonometric force model and use differentiation to minimize the required force.
questions.accessibleText:
9. [Maximum mark: 15]

Eleanor uses the handle on a heavy suitcase to pull it so that it moves horizontally along the floor.

The handle makes an angle of θ radians with the horizontal, as shown in the following diagram.

[Diagram not to scale: A rectangular suitcase rests on a horizontal floor. Its handle extends upwards and to the right, making an angle θ with a dashed horizontal line at the handle attachment point. A horizontal arrow points right from the suitcase.]

The magnitude, F Newtons, of the minimum force that Eleanor needs to apply to make the suitcase move horizontally when the handle makes an angle of θ radians is given by

F(θ) = A/(cos θ + μ sin θ), where 0 ≤ θ < π/2 and μ ∈ ℝ.

When the handle is horizontal, F = 300.

(a) Show that A = 300. [2]

In the case when θ = π/6, F = 100√3.

(b) Show that μ = √3. [4]

Eleanor wishes to minimize the magnitude of the force she needs to apply to make the suitcase move horizontally. In order to achieve this, she needs to hold the handle at the angle α, where 0 < α < π/2.

(c) (i) Show that dF/dθ = 300(sin θ − √3 cos θ)/(cos θ + √3 sin θ)².
    (ii) Hence, show that α = π/3 and find the corresponding value of F(α). [9]
questions.solution: The model is F(θ)=A/(cos θ+μ sin θ), for 0≤θ<π/2. (a) F(0)=A=300, hence A=300. (b) Using F(π/6)=100√3 gives 300/(√3/2+μ/2)=100√3. Thus 600/(√3+μ)=100√3, so √3+μ=2√3 and μ=√3. (c)(i) Therefore F(θ)=300(cos θ+√3 sin θ)^(−1), and differentiation gives F′(θ)=300(sin θ−√3 cos θ)/(cos θ+√3 sin θ)². (ii) At an interior minimum F′(α)=0, so tan α=√3. Since 0<α<π/2, α=π/3. The derivative changes from negative to positive there, confirming a minimum. Finally F(π/3)=300/(1/2+√3·√3/2)=300/2=150 N.

questions.summary: Use proportional stratified sampling and a box plot of weekly allowances to find a stratum size, quartiles, and an outlier boundary.
questions.accessibleText:
1. [Maximum mark: 6]

A school has 600 students across four grade levels as shown in the following table.

[Table: Grade 9, 115 students; Grade 10, 178 students; Grade 11, 137 students; Grade 12, 170 students.]

A group of 60 students was surveyed using a stratified sampling technique, such that each grade in the sample was proportional to the population. Each student was asked how much allowance, in Singapore dollars ($), they received per week.

(a) Find the number of Grade 12 students in the sample. [2]

The results of the survey are summarized in the following box and whisker diagram.

[Box-and-whisker diagram titled ‘Survey of allowances from 60 students’: minimum 28, lower quartile 66, median 80, upper quartile a, and maximum 110.]

(b) State the median. [1]

The interquartile range is $24.

(c) Write down the value of a. [1]

An outlier is a value that is less than Q₁ − 1.5 × IQR or greater than Q₃ + 1.5 × IQR.

(d) Determine the smallest possible allowance, from the sample, that is not an outlier. [2]
questions.solution: (a) Grade 12 contributes (170/600)×60 = 17 students. (b) The median line is at $80. (c) Q₁=66 and IQR=24, so Q₃=a=66+24=90. (d) The lower outlier fence is Q₁−1.5(IQR)=66−1.5(24)=30. Values below 30 are outliers, so the smallest possible non-outlier allowance is $30.
questions.solutionStatus: Independent worked solution — not an official IB markscheme

questions.summary: Find a triangle side and area from two sides and the cosine of their included acute angle.
questions.accessibleText:
2. [Maximum mark: 7]

The following diagram shows triangle ABC. It is known that AB = 5 cm, BC = 6 cm, and cos ∠ABC = 1/5 where ∠ABC is acute.

[Diagram not to scale: triangle ABC with B at the top, A at the lower left and C at the lower right; side AB is labelled 5 and side BC is labelled 6.]

(a) Find AC. [3]

(b) (i) Show that sin ∠ABC = 2√6/5.

(ii) Hence, find the area of triangle ABC. [4]
questions.solution: (a) By the cosine rule, AC²=5²+6²−2(5)(6)(1/5)=49, hence AC=7 cm. (b)(i) Since angle B is acute, sin B=√(1−cos²B)=√(1−1/25)=2√6/5. (ii) Area = (1/2)(5)(6)sin B = 6√6 cm².
questions.solutionStatus: Independent worked solution — not an official IB markscheme

questions.summary: Compare two coefficients in the expansion of (1+mx)⁸ and determine the positive parameter m.
questions.accessibleText:
3. [Maximum mark: 6]

Consider the expansion of (1 + mx)⁸, where m ∈ ℝ and m > 0.

The coefficient of x³ is eight times the coefficient of x².

(a) Show that ⁸C₃ = 56. [1]

(b) Find the value of m. [5]
questions.solution: (a) ⁸C₃=8!/(3!5!)=(8·7·6)/(3·2·1)=56. (b) The x³ and x² coefficients are 56m³ and ⁸C₂m²=28m². Thus 56m³=8(28m²). Since m>0, divide by 56m² to obtain m=4.
questions.solutionStatus: Independent worked solution — not an official IB markscheme

questions.summary: Use logarithm laws and integer restrictions to solve two simultaneous logarithmic equations.
questions.accessibleText:
4. [Maximum mark: 6]

In this question, p and r are positive integers greater than 1.

(a) Given that log₃ p = 3 + log₃ r, show that p = 27r. [2]

(b) Hence, find the value of r and the value of p that satisfy these simultaneous equations:

log₃ p = 3 + log₃ r
logᵣ p = 4. [4]
questions.solution: (a) log₃p=3+log₃r=log₃27+log₃r=log₃(27r), so p=27r. (b) logᵣp=4 gives p=r⁴. Hence r⁴=27r, and because r>1, r³=27, so r=3 and p=81.
questions.solutionStatus: Independent worked solution — not an official IB markscheme

questions.summary: Differentiate x⁴−sin(4x), then recognize a reverse-chain-rule antiderivative involving its seventh power.
questions.accessibleText:
5. [Maximum mark: 5]

Let y = x⁴ − sin 4x.

(a) Find dy/dx. [2]

(b) Hence, or otherwise, find ∫(x⁴ − sin 4x)⁷(x³ − cos 4x) dx. [3]
questions.solution: (a) dy/dx=4x³−4cos(4x)=4(x³−cos(4x)). (b) Let u=x⁴−sin(4x), so du=4(x³−cos(4x))dx. Therefore ∫(x⁴−sin(4x))⁷(x³−cos(4x))dx=(1/4)∫u⁷du=u⁸/32+C=(x⁴−sin(4x))⁸/32+C.

questions.summary: Analyze a downward-opening quadratic in factored and vertex forms, find a secant-line parameter, and classify roots as a level varies.
questions.accessibleText:
7. [Maximum mark: 14]

Consider the quadratic function f(x) = −(x + 2)(x − 4), for x ∈ ℝ. The following diagram shows part of the graph of f.

[Coordinate diagram with horizontal x-axis and vertical y-axis: the graph is a downward-opening parabola whose vertex is above and to the right of the y-axis, with one x-intercept to the left of the y-axis and one to the right.]

(a) (i) Find the x-coordinate of each of the x-intercepts.

(ii) Find the coordinates of the vertex. [5]

The function f can also be written in the form f(x) = −(x − h)² + k, where h, k ∈ ℝ.

(b) Write down the value of

(i) h;

(ii) k. [2]

The line y = mx + 4, where m ∈ ℝ, intersects the graph of f at x = −2 and x = 2.

(c) Determine the value of m. [3]

Consider the equation −x² + 2x + 8 − p = 0, where p ∈ ℝ.

(d) By considering the graph of f, or otherwise, find the range of possible values of p such that this equation has

(i) two distinct real roots;

(ii) two distinct positive real roots. [4]
questions.solution: Write f(x)=−(x+2)(x−4)=−x²+2x+8=−(x−1)²+9. (a)(i) The x-intercepts have x=−2 and x=4. (a)(ii) The vertex is (1,9). (b)(i) Therefore h=1. (b)(ii) Therefore k=9. (c) At x=−2, f(−2)=0, so −2m+4=0 and m=2 (also consistent at x=2). (d)(i) The equation is f(x)=p; a horizontal line y=p meets the parabola twice exactly when p<9. (d)(ii) Both intersections are positive when the level lies above f(0)=8 but below the maximum, hence 8<p<9.
questions.solutionStatus: Independent worked solution — not an official IB markscheme

questions.summary: Solve and sketch the intersections of sin(2x) and 1−cos(2x), then integrate the area between two nonzero intersections.
questions.accessibleText:
8. [Maximum mark: 16]

The functions f and g are defined for 0 ≤ x ≤ π by

f(x) = sin 2x
g(x) = 1 − cos 2x.

(a) Solve the equation f(x) = g(x) for 0 ≤ x ≤ π. [6]

(b) Sketch the graphs of y = f(x) and y = g(x) on the same set of axes, clearly labelling the points of intersection with their coordinates. [4]

The graphs of f and g intersect at x = a and x = b, where 0 < a < b.

(c) Find the area of the region enclosed by the graphs of f and g for a ≤ x ≤ b. [6]
questions.solution: (a) sin(2x)=1−cos(2x) becomes 2sin x cos x=2sin²x, so 2sin x(cos x−sin x)=0. On 0≤x≤π, x=0, π/4, π. (b) Intersections are (0,0), (π/4,1), and (π,0). For the sketch, f has zeros at 0, π/2, π, maximum (π/4,1), and minimum (3π/4,−1); g has zeros at 0 and π and maximum (π/2,2). (c) The positive intersections are a=π/4 and b=π, and g≥f between them. Area = ∫[π/4 to π](1−cos(2x)−sin(2x))dx = [x−(1/2)sin(2x)+(1/2)cos(2x)] from π/4 to π = 3π/4+1.
questions.solutionStatus: Independent worked solution — not an official IB markscheme

questions.summary: Differentiate an exponential quotient to study monotonicity, find a normal, and prove the curve has no inflection point.
questions.accessibleText:
9. [Maximum mark: 14]

Consider the function h(x) = (e²ˣ + x)/x, for x > 0.

(a) Show that h′(x) = e²ˣ(2x − 1)/x². [4]

(b) Find the values of x for which h is an increasing function. [2]

(c) Find the equation of the normal to the curve y = h(x) at the point (1, e² + 1). [4]

The second derivative of h is given by h″(x) = 2e²ˣ(2x² − 2x + 1)/x³.

(d) Show that the graph of h does not have a point of inflexion. [4]
questions.solution: For x>0, h(x)=(e^(2x)+x)/x. (a) The quotient rule gives h′(x)=[x(2e^(2x)+1)−(e^(2x)+x)]/x²=e^(2x)(2x−1)/x². (b) Since e^(2x)/x²>0, h′(x)>0 exactly when x>1/2. (c) h′(1)=e², so the normal slope is −e^(−2). Its equation is y−(e²+1)=−e^(−2)(x−1). (d) The supplied h″ has sign determined by 2x²−2x+1=2(x−1/2)²+1/2>0. All other factors in h″ are positive for x>0, so h″(x)>0 throughout the domain and concavity never changes; therefore there is no point of inflection.
questions.solutionStatus: Independent worked solution — not an official IB markscheme

questions.summary: Evaluate an exponential cooling model for a cup of tea and identify its limiting room temperature.
questions.accessibleText:
1. [Maximum mark: 5]

Jane makes a cup of tea and forgets to drink it so that it cools towards the temperature of the room.

The temperature T °C of the cup of tea after t minutes is given by T(t) = 18 + 72e^(−(1/20)t).

(a) Find the initial temperature of the tea. [2]

(b) Find the temperature of the tea after 15 minutes. [2]

(c) Write down the temperature of the room. [1]

questions.summary: Compare quarterly compound-interest growth with annual boat depreciation to determine affordability.
questions.accessibleText:
8. [Maximum mark: 13]

At the start of 2026, Lavinia receives a gift of $15 000. She wants to buy a boat which costs $28 000 so she decides to invest her money.

On 1 January 2026 Lavinia invests her money in a bank account which pays interest at a nominal annual rate of 4.8%, compounded quarterly. The interest is paid into her account on the last day of each quarter. She makes no further deposits to, or withdrawals from, the account.

(a) Find the amount of money Lavinia will have in her bank account on 1 January 2031. Give your answer correct to the nearest dollar. [3]

(b) Show that Lavinia will first have more than $28 000 in her bank account during the year 2039. [3]

The cost of the boat at the start of 2026 was $28 000, and it depreciates at a constant annual rate of r%. After one year the cost of the boat is $26 222.

(c) Find the value of r. [2]

Due to this depreciation, Lavinia will be able to buy the boat before 2039. She will buy the boat as soon as she has enough money in her bank account to pay for it.

(d) Determine the year during which Lavinia will buy the boat. [5]
questions.solution: The quarterly multiplier is 1+0.048/4=1.012. (a) From 1 Jan 2026 to 1 Jan 2031 there are 20 quarters, so the balance is 15000(1.012)^20=$19041.52≈$19042. (b) 15000(1.012)^n>28000 requires n>ln(28000/15000)/ln(1.012)=52.324, so the first qualifying payment is quarter 53, during 2039. (c) 26222=28000(1−r/100), giving r=6.35%. (d) After t years, compare 15000(1.012)^{4t} with 28000(0.9365)^t. Equality gives t=ln(28000/15000)/ln[(1.012)^4/0.9365]=5.51 years after 1 January 2026. The first quarterly account credit after this crossing is at t=5.75 years, still during 2031; therefore she buys during 2031.

The waiting time, T minutes, of patients at a clinic can be modelled by a normal distribution with mean μ and standard deviation σ. The waiting times of all patients are independent of each other.

3.8% of the patients have a waiting time of less than 20 minutes, while 7.3% of the patients have a waiting time of more than 30 minutes.

(a) (i) Find the value of μ and the value of σ.

(ii) Hence, find the probability that a patient chosen at random has a waiting time of between 15 and 22 minutes. [7]

The doctor at the clinic only sees patients with an appointment.

Records show that 82.6% of patients attend their appointment.

The probability of a patient attending their appointment is independent of any other patient.

(b) On a particular day, 20 patients each made an appointment to see the doctor.

(i) Find the probability that at least 13 of these patients attended their appointment.

(ii) Given that at least 13 of these patients attended their appointment, find the probability that more than 2 patients did not attend their appointment. [7]
questions.solution: Let T~N(μ,σ²). (a)(i) Φ((20−μ)/σ)=0.038 and Φ((30−μ)/σ)=0.927. Using z=−1.774 and 1.454 gives μ=25.5 min and σ=3.10 min. (ii) P(15<T<22)=Φ((22−μ)/σ)−Φ((15−μ)/σ)=0.129. (b) Let X~Bin(20,0.826) count attendees. (i) P(X≥13)=1−P(X≤12)=0.985. (ii) More than 2 fail means X≤17; conditional on X≥13, the probability is P(13≤X≤17)/P(X≥13)=0.697.

questions.summary: Relate geometric sequences and their sums to a logarithmically transformed arithmetic sequence.

9. [Maximum mark: 15]

The geometric sequence a₁, a₂, a₃, … has common ratio r. The sum to infinity, A∞, of this sequence is 5.

(a) Find an expression for a₁ in terms of r. [1]

A second geometric sequence a₁², a₂², a₃², … has common ratio q.

(b) Show that q = r². [2]

The sum to infinity, B∞, of this second sequence is 16.

(c) (i) Show that 41r² − 50r + 9 = 0.

(ii) Find the value of r.

(iii) Hence, find the value of a₁. [5]

A third sequence has its nth term given by cₙ = logₖ(aₙ) + k, where k ∈ ℤ⁺, k > 1.

(d) Show that this third sequence is arithmetic. [4]

Let C₂₀ denote the sum of the first 20 terms of the third sequence.

(e) Find the maximum value of k such that C₂₀ < 0. [3]
questions.solution: (a) Since a₁/(1−r)=5, a₁=5(1−r). (b) The ratio of aₙ² is a_{n+1}²/aₙ²=r², so q=r². (c)(i) Its sum is a₁²/(1−r²)=16. Substituting a₁=5(1−r) gives 25(1−r)/(1+r)=16, hence 41r²−50r+9=0. (c)(ii) The roots are 1 and 9/41; convergence excludes 1, so r=9/41. (c)(iii) Therefore a₁=5(1−9/41)=160/41. (d) cₙ=log_k(a₁r^{n−1})+k=log_k(a₁)+(n−1)log_k(r)+k, so it is arithmetic with common difference log_k(r). (e) C₂₀=20[log_k(a₁)+k]+190log_k(r). questions.solution: Since P(A′) = 3/4, P(A) = 1 − 3/4 = 1/4. (a) By conditional probability, P(B | A) = P(A ∩ B)/P(A). Thus P(A ∩ B) = P(B | A)P(A) = (2/3)(1/4) = 1/6. (b) Using P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B), 3/4 = 1/4 + P(B) − 1/6. Hence P(B) = 3/4 − 1/4 + 1/6 = 2/3. Therefore P(A)P(B) = (1/4)(2/3) = 1/6 = P(A ∩ B), so A and B are independent.

7. [Maximum mark: 13]

An object moves in a straight line.

Its velocity v m s⁻¹, at time t seconds, is given by v(t) = 30 + 20t − 10t² for 0 ≤ t ≤ 5.

The graph of v is shown in the following diagram.

[Diagram: A velocity-time graph with horizontal axis t marked 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and vertical axis v(t). The graph is a downward-opening parabola. It starts above the t-axis at t = 0 with v(0) = 30, rises to its local and absolute maximum at t = 1 with v(1) = 40, then falls, intersects the t-axis at t = 3, and continues below the axis to t = 5, where v(5) = −120.]

The graph of v has a local maximum point where t = 1 and intersects the t-axis at t = 3.

(a) Determine the object’s
    (i) maximum velocity;
    (ii) maximum speed. [4]

At t = T, the object changes direction.

(b) (i) Write down the value of T.
    (ii) Find the distance travelled by the object in the first T seconds. [5]

(c) Determine whether the object returns to its initial position during the time period 0 ≤ t ≤ 5, justifying your answer. [4]
questions.solution: (a)(i) The downward-opening velocity graph has its maximum at t = 1. Thus the maximum velocity is v(1) = 30 + 20 − 10 = 40 m s⁻¹. (ii) Speed is |v|. At t = 5, v(5) = 30 + 100 − 250 = −120 m s⁻¹, whose magnitude is 120 m s⁻¹; this exceeds 40 m s⁻¹, so the maximum speed is 120 m s⁻¹. (b)(i) The object changes direction when velocity changes sign, at the given intercept t = 3; hence T = 3. (ii) Since v ≥ 0 from t = 0 to t = 3, the distance travelled is ∫₀³(30 + 20t − 10t²) dt = [30t + 10t² − (10/3)t³]₀³ = 90 + 90 − 90 = 90 m. (c) The displacement by t = 5 is ∫₀⁵v(t)dt = [30t + 10t² − (10/3)t³]₀⁵ = 150 + 250 − 1250/3 = −50/3 m. At t = 3 the displacement is 90 m, while at t = 5 it is negative. Since displacement is continuous, it must equal zero at some time between 3 and 5. Therefore the object does return to its initial position during 0 ≤ t ≤ 5.

questions.summary: Rewrite and sketch a quadratic, solve its inequality, and transfer the result through a logarithmic composition.

8. [Maximum mark: 15]

The function f is defined by f(x) = 5(x + 1)(x + 3), where x ∈ ℝ.

(a) Write f(x) in the form a(x − h)² + k, where a, h, k ∈ ℤ. [4]

(b) Sketch the graph of y = f(x), showing the values of any intercepts with the axes and the coordinates of the vertex. [4]

(c) Solve the inequality f(x) ≤ 40. [4]

The function g is defined by g(x) = ln x, where x ∈ ℝ, x > 0.

(d) (i) Write down an expression for (f ∘ g)(x).
    (ii) Solve the inequality (f ∘ g)(x) ≤ 40. [3]
questions.solution: (a) f(x) = 5(x² + 4x + 3) = 5[(x + 2)² − 1] = 5(x + 2)² − 5. Thus a = 5, h = −2 and k = −5. (b) The graph is an upward-opening parabola. From the factorized form its x-intercepts are (−3, 0) and (−1, 0). Its y-intercept is (0, 15), and its vertex is (−2, −5), with axis of symmetry x = −2. (c) 5(x + 2)² − 5 ≤ 40 gives (x + 2)² ≤ 9, so −3 ≤ x + 2 ≤ 3 and therefore −5 ≤ x ≤ 1. (d)(i) (f ∘ g)(x) = f(ln x) = 5(ln x + 1)(ln x + 3), for x > 0. (ii) Applying part (c) with ln x in place of x gives −5 ≤ ln x ≤ 1. Since the exponential function is increasing, e⁻⁵ ≤ x ≤ e.

questions.summary: Use inscribed-cylinder geometry, surface areas and trigonometry to derive the cylinder’s volume.
questions.accessibleText:
9. [Maximum mark: 17]

A solid cylinder has height h cm and base radius R cm.

The cylinder fits exactly inside a hollow sphere of radius r cm.

Points A, B and C are points where the surface of the cylinder touches the surface of the sphere.

The line segment [AB] is a diameter of the sphere.

The line segment [BC] is a diameter of the base of the cylinder and AB̂C = θ.

This information is shown on the following diagram.

[Diagram not to scale: A vertical solid cylinder fits exactly inside a hollow sphere, shown in cross-section as a rectangle inside a circle with elliptical top and bottom faces. A is the upper-left contact point of the cylinder and sphere, C is the lower-left contact point, and B is the lower-right contact point. Segment AC is vertical and is labelled h; it is the cylinder’s height. Segment BC runs across the bottom base from C to B and is its diameter, of length 2R. Dashed segment AB runs diagonally from A to B and is a diameter of the sphere, of length 2r. Triangle ABC is right-angled at C. The angle ABC between BA and BC is labelled θ. Above the cylinder, horizontal dimension arrows from the vertical centreline to the right-hand surfaces label the sphere radius r and the cylinder base radius R.]

(a) (i) By considering triangle ABC, show that R = r cos θ.
    (ii) Find an expression for h in terms of r and θ. [4]

(b) Hence or otherwise, show that the total surface area, S cm², of the cylinder is given by S = 2πr²(1 + 2 sin θ cos θ − sin²θ). [4]

The external surface area of the sphere is 2S.

(c) Show that tan θ = 2. [4]

The volume of the cylinder is V cm³.

(d) Find V, giving your answer in the form pπr³√5, where p ∈ ℚ⁺. [5]
questions.solution: (a)(i) Since AB is the sphere’s diameter, AB = 2r. Since BC is the cylinder base’s diameter, BC = 2R. In right triangle ABC, cos θ = BC/AB = 2R/(2r) = R/r, so R = r cos θ. (ii) AC is the cylinder height h and is opposite θ, so sin θ = h/(2r), giving h = 2r sin θ. (b) The cylinder’s total surface area is the area of its two circular ends plus its curved surface: S = 2πR² + 2πRh. Substituting R = r cos θ and h = 2r sin θ gives S = 2πr²cos²θ + 4πr²sin θ cos θ = 2πr²(cos²θ + 2 sin θ cos θ). Since cos²θ = 1 − sin²θ, S = 2πr²(1 + 2 sin θ cos θ − sin²θ), as required. (c) The sphere’s external surface area is 4πr², and this equals 2S. Hence 4πr² = 4πr²(1 + 2 sin θ cos θ − sin²θ), so 2 sin θ cos θ − sin²θ = 0. As θ is an acute angle, sin θ ≠ 0; dividing by sin θ cos θ gives 2 − tan θ = 0. Therefore tan θ = 2. (d) V = πR²h = π(r cos θ)²(2r sin θ) = 2πr³sin θ cos²θ. From tan θ = 2, take the sides of a right triangle proportional to 2, 1 and √5, so sin θ = 2/√5 and cos θ = 1/√5. Thus V = 2πr³(2/√5)(1/5) = 4πr³/(5√5) = (4/25)πr³√5. Therefore p = 4/25.

[Diagram: Coordinate axes are labelled x and y, with arrowheads in both directions and no numerical tick labels. The rational graph has two increasing branches. Its vertical asymptote is x = −1/2 and its horizontal asymptote is y = 3/2. The left branch lies above y = 3/2 and tends upward as x approaches −1/2 from the left. The right branch tends downward as x approaches −1/2 from the right, passes through (0, −2), crosses the x-axis at (2/3, 0), and approaches y = 3/2 from below.]

diagram not to scale

[Diagram: Triangle ABC has A at the lower left, C at the lower right and B above A. AC is horizontal. Side AB is labelled 5 and side BC is labelled 6√2. The interior angle BÂC at A is labelled 2θ, and the interior angle AĈB at C is labelled θ.]

(a) Using the sine rule, show that cos θ = 3√2/5. [3]

(b) Hence, find sin θ. [2]

Point D is located on [AC] such that the area of triangle BCD is 2√14.

(c) Find DC. [2]
questions.solution: (a) The sine rule gives sin θ/5 = sin(2θ)/(6√2). Using sin(2θ) = 2sin θ cos θ and cancelling sin θ (which is positive) gives 1/5 = 2cos θ/(6√2), hence cos θ = 3√2/5. (b) Since 0 < θ < π/2, sin θ is positive. Thus sin θ = √(1 − cos²θ) = √(1 − 18/25) = √7/5. (c) Triangle BCD has included angle θ between BC and DC, so 2√14 = ½(6√2)(DC)(√7/5) = (3√14/5)DC. Therefore DC = 10/3.

5. [Maximum mark: 7]

The quadratic equation x² + kx + 15 − k = 0 has two distinct real roots.

(a) Find the possible values of k. [5]

(b) Find the possible values of k in the case where the two distinct real roots are both positive or both negative. [2]
questions.solution: (a) Distinct real roots require Δ > 0. Here Δ = k² − 4(15 − k) = k² + 4k − 60 = (k + 10)(k − 6). Therefore k < −10 or k > 6. (b) For the roots to have the same sign, their product 15 − k must be positive, so k < 15. Intersecting this with the result from part (a) gives k < −10 or 6 < k < 15.

6. [Maximum mark: 7]

Consider the function f(x) = √(x² ln x + 4 − x²), where x ∈ ℝ, x > 0.

(a) Show that the distance, l, between the origin and any point on the graph of f is given by l = √(x² ln x + 4). [1]

(b) Hence, find the x-coordinate of the point on the graph of f which is closest to the origin. [6]
questions.solution: (a) A point on the graph is (x, f(x)), so l = √(x² + f(x)²) = √(x² + x²ln x + 4 − x²) = √(x²ln x + 4). (b) Since the square-root function is increasing, minimise l² = x²ln x + 4. Its derivative is 2xln x + x = x(2ln x + 1). Because x > 0, a stationary point satisfies 2ln x + 1 = 0, so ln x = −1/2 and x = e⁻¹ᐟ² = 1/√e. Also, d²(l²)/dx² = 2ln x + 3, which equals 2 > 0 at x = e⁻¹ᐟ²; therefore this point gives the minimum distance. The required x-coordinate is 1/√e.

7. [Maximum mark: 13]

A discrete random variable, X, has the following probability distribution, where a > 0 and k is a constant.

[Table: The first row is headed x and contains 0, a, 2a, 3a. The second row is headed P(X = x) and contains, respectively, k, 3k², 2k², k².]

(a) Show that k = 1/3. [5]

(b) Find P(X < 3a). [2]

(c) Find P(X ≥ a | X < 3a). [3]

(d) Given that E(X) = 20, find the value of a. [3]
questions.solution: (a) The probabilities sum to 1, so k + 3k² + 2k² + k² = 1, giving 6k² + k − 1 = 0. Factoring, (3k − 1)(2k + 1) = 0, so k = 1/3 or k = −1/2. Since k is a probability and must be non-negative, k = 1/3. (b) P(X < 3a) = k + 3k² + 2k² = 1/3 + 5/9 = 8/9. (c) Under X < 3a, the outcomes satisfying X ≥ a are a and 2a. Therefore P(X ≥ a | X < 3a) = (3k² + 2k²)/(8/9) = (5/9)/(8/9) = 5/8. (d) E(X) = 0(k) + a(3k²) + 2a(2k²) + 3a(k²). With k = 1/3, E(X) = 3a/9 + 4a/9 + 3a/9 = 10a/9. Hence 10a/9 = 20, so a = 18.

8. [Maximum mark: 15]

A Ferris wheel with diameter 72 metres rotates at a constant speed. The lowest point on the wheel is 8 metres above the ground, as shown on the following diagram. A seat starts at the lowest point.

[Diagram: A circular Ferris wheel is supported above a horizontal line labelled ground by two sloping supports meeting at its centre. A horizontal double-headed arrow through the centre spans the wheel and is labelled 72 metres. A vertical double-headed arrow from the ground to the lowest point of the wheel is labelled 8 metres. A curved arrow on the left of the wheel points upward, indicating anticlockwise rotation. The seat starts at the lowest point of the circle.]

The wheel completes one revolution in 12 minutes.

After t minutes, the height, h metres, of the seat above the ground is given by h(t) = a cos(bt) + 44, where a, b ∈ ℝ.

(a) Find the value of
    (i) a;
    (ii) b. [4]

(b) Sketch the graph of h, for 0 ≤ t ≤ 12. Clearly label the coordinates of the maximum point and the end points. [2]

Consider one revolution of the Ferris wheel.

(c) The seat is at least 26 m above the ground for T minutes. Find the value of T. [5]

(d) (i) Find h′(t).
    (ii) Hence or otherwise, find the time at which the height of the seat above the ground is decreasing at its fastest rate. [4]
questions.solution: (a) (i) At t = 0 the seat is at height 8, so a cos 0 + 44 = 8 and a = −36. (ii) The period is 12, so 2π/b = 12 and b = π/6. Thus h(t) = −36cos(πt/6) + 44. (b) Over 0 ≤ t ≤ 12, the graph is one cosine cycle with end points (0, 8) and (12, 8), and maximum point (6, 80). (c) The condition h(t) ≥ 26 gives −36cos(πt/6) + 44 ≥ 26, or cos(πt/6) ≤ 1/2. During one revolution this holds from t = 2 to t = 10, so T = 10 − 2 = 8 minutes. (d) (i) h′(t) = 6πsin(πt/6). (ii) The height decreases fastest when h′ is as negative as possible, namely when sin(πt/6) = −1. In 0 ≤ t ≤ 12 this occurs at πt/6 = 3π/2, giving t = 9 minutes.

9. [Maximum mark: 17]

The function f is defined by f(x) = 4ˣ, where x ∈ ℝ.

(a) Find f⁻¹(8). Express your answer in the form p/q where p, q ∈ ℤ. [3]

The function g is defined by g(x) = 1 + log₂ x, where x ∈ ℝ⁺.

(b) (i) Find an expression for g⁻¹(x).
    (ii) Describe a sequence of transformations that transforms the graph of y = g⁻¹(x) to the graph of y = f(x). [4]

(c) Show that (f ◦ g)(x) = 4x². [3]

The function h is defined by h(x) = 4x²/(2x + 1), x ≠ −1/2.

The following diagram shows part of the graph of h. Let R be the region enclosed by the graph of h and the x-axis, between the lines x = 1 and x = 3.

[Diagram: Coordinate axes are labelled x and y and marked with evenly spaced, unnumbered ticks. The positive branch of the curve h begins at the origin, rises and is concave up in the displayed interval. Vertical boundary segments are drawn from the x-axis to the curve at x = 1 and x = 3, with filled points on the x-axis labelled 1 and 3. The region under h, above the x-axis and between these boundaries is shaded grey and labelled R.]

(d) (i) Show that 2x − 1 + 1/(2x + 1) = 4x²/(2x + 1).
    (ii) Hence or otherwise, find the area of R, giving your answer in the form p + q ln r, where p, q, r ∈ ℚ⁺. [7]
questions.solution: (a) Let f⁻¹(8) = x. Then 4ˣ = 8, so 2²ˣ = 2³ and x = 3/2. (b) (i) From y = 1 + log₂x, interchange x and y: x = 1 + log₂y, so y = 2ˣ⁻¹. Therefore g⁻¹(x) = 2ˣ⁻¹. (ii) First translate the graph of y = g⁻¹(x) one unit to the left, obtaining y = 2ˣ. Then apply a horizontal stretch with scale factor 1/2 (equivalently, a horizontal compression by factor 2), obtaining y = 2²ˣ = 4ˣ = f(x). (c) (f ◦ g)(x) = 4^(1 + log₂x) = 4(2²)^(log₂x) = 4(2^(log₂x))² = 4x². (d) (i) Putting the left side over the common denominator 2x + 1 gives [(2x − 1)(2x + 1) + 1]/(2x + 1) = (4x² − 1 + 1)/(2x + 1) = 4x²/(2x + 1). (ii) The area is ∫₁³h(x) dx = ∫₁³[2x − 1 + 1/(2x + 1)] dx. An antiderivative is x² − x + ½ln(2x + 1). Hence the area is [x² − x + ½ln(2x + 1)]₁³ = (6 + ½ln 7) − ½ln 3 = 6 + ½ln(7/3).

6. [Maximum mark: 6]

The random variables X and Y are normally distributed with X ∼ N(7, a²) and Y ∼ N(19, a²), where a > 0.

(a) Find b such that P(X > b) = P(Y > 22). [2]

(b) Write down the approximate value of P(7 − a < X < 7 + a), correct to two significant figures. [1]

(c) Given that a = 3, calculate the approximate value of P(Y < 22), correct to two significant figures. [3]
questions.solution: (a) Since X and Y have the same variance, P(X > b) = P(Y > 22) means b is as many standard deviations above 7 as 22 is above 19. So b − 7 = 22 − 19 = 3, hence b = 10. (b) By the empirical rule, P(μ − σ < X < μ + σ) ≈ 0.68 (or 68%). (c) For Y ∼ N(19, 9), 22 is one standard deviation above the mean. P(Y < 22) = 0.5 + P(19 < Y < 22) ≈ 0.5 + 0.34 = 0.84 (correct to 2 significant figures).

    (iii) Find the value of y when x = k. [7]

(e) (i) Find an expression for d²T/dx².
    (ii) Hence, justify whether T has a local minimum or a local maximum when x = k. [2]
questions.solution: (a) The total area is 8xy = 60, so y = 60/(8x) = 15/(2x). (b) The rope consists of 3 horizontal segments each of length 4x (total 12x) and 5 vertical segments each of length 2y (total 10y). So T = 12x + 10y = 12x + 10(15/(2x)) = 12x + 75/x. (c) dT/dx = 12 − 75/x². (d) (i) Setting 12 − 75/k² = 0 gives k² = 75/12 = 25/4, so k = 5/2 (since x > 0). (ii) T = 12(5/2) + 75/(5/2) = 30 + 30 = 60 m. (iii) y = 15/(2 × 5/2) = 15/5 = 3 m. (e) (i) d²T/dx² = 150/x³. (ii) At x = 5/2, d²T/dx² = 150/(125/8) = 150 × 8/125 = 48/5 = 9.6 > 0, so T has a local minimum at x = k.

questions.summary: Investigate a sequence for arithmetic and geometric conditions, analyse convergence, and find the sum of an even number of terms.
questions.accessibleText:
8. [Maximum mark: 16]

Consider the sequence {uₙ}, with nth term given by uₙ. The first three terms are u₁ = k − 5, u₂ = 3 − 2k and u₃ = 5k + 3, where k ∈ ℝ.

(a) Consider the case when {uₙ} is arithmetic.
    (i) Find the value of k.
    (ii) Hence, or otherwise, find u₃. [5]

(b) Consider the case where k = 12.
    (i) Show that the first three terms of {uₙ} form a geometric sequence.
    (ii) Given that {uₙ} is geometric, state a reason why the sum of an infinite number of terms of this sequence does not exist. [4]

(c) The sequence, {uₙ}, is geometric for a second value of k.
    (i) Show that k² − 10k − 24 = 0.
    (ii) Find the first three terms of {uₙ} for this second value of k.
    (iii) Hence, write down the value of S₂ₘ, the sum of the first 2m terms, for this second value of k. [7]
questions.solution: (a) (i) For an arithmetic sequence, u₂ − u₁ = u₃ − u₂. So (3 − 2k) − (k − 5) = (5k + 3) − (3 − 2k). This gives 3 − 2k − k + 5 = 5k + 3 − 3 + 2k, so 8 − 3k = 7k, hence 8 = 10k, so k = 4/5. (ii) u₃ = 5(4/5) + 3 = 4 + 3 = 7. (b) (i) When k = 12: u₁ = 12 − 5 = 7, u₂ = 3 − 2(12) = 3 − 24 = −21, u₃ = 5(12) + 3 = 60 + 3 = 63. The common ratio is r = u₂/u₁ = −21/7 = −3 and u₃/u₂ = 63/(−21) = −3, so the three terms form a geometric sequence with r = −3. (ii) The sum of an infinite number of terms does not exist because |r| = 3 ≥ 1, so the series diverges. (c) (i) For a geometric sequence, u₂² = u₁u₃. So (3 − 2k)² = (k − 5)(5k + 3). Expanding: 4k² − 12k + 9 = 5k² + 3k − 25k − 15 = 5k² − 22k − 15. Rearranging: 0 = k² − 10k − 24. (ii) k² − 10k − 24 = (k − 12)(k + 2) = 0, so k = −2 (the second value, since k = 12 was already considered). u₁ = −2 − 5 = −7, u₂ = 3 − 2(−2) = 3 + 4 = 7, u₃ = 5(−2) + 3 = −10 + 3 = −7. The terms are −7, 7, −7, ... with r = −1. (iii) S₂ₘ = 0 because the terms cancel in pairs: (−7 + 7) + (−7 + 7) + ... + (−7 + 7) = 0.

questions.summary: Analyse a logarithmic function with a quadratic argument: find domain, zeros, and determine the base from the maximum value.
questions.accessibleText:
9. [Maximum mark: 16]

(a) (i) Solve 5 − 4x − x² = 0.
    (ii) Hence, find the values of x such that 5 − 4x − x² > 0. [4]

Consider the function f(x) = logₖ(5 − 4x − x²), where a < x < b and k > 1. Part of the graph of f is shown in the following diagram.

[Diagram: A coordinate grid showing the graph of y = f(x). The curve has vertical asymptotes at x = a and x = b, and lies between them. The curve rises from the left asymptote to a maximum point, then decreases to the right asymptote. The maximum point is labelled as having y-coordinate 2.]

(b) Write down the value of
    (i) a;
    (ii) b. [2]

(c) Find the exact values of x such that f(x) = 0. [4]

The graph of f has a maximum value of 2.

(d) Find the value of k. [6]
questions.solution: (a) (i) 5 − 4x − x² = 0 ⇒ x² + 4x − 5 = 0 ⇒ (x + 5)(x − 1) = 0 ⇒ x = −5 or x = 1. (ii) The quadratic is a negative parabola (opening downwards) with roots at −5 and 1, so 5 − 4x − x² > 0 when −5 < x < 1. (b) The domain of f is a < x < b, which corresponds to the interval where the argument is positive. So a = −5 and b = 1. (c) f(x) = 0 when logₖ(5 − 4x − x²) = 0 ⇒ 5 − 4x − x² = 1 ⇒ x² + 4x − 4 = 0. Using the quadratic formula: x = [−4 ± √(16 + 16)]/2 = [−4 ± √32]/2 = [−4 ± 4√2]/2 = −2 ± 2√2. (d) The maximum of f occurs at the maximum of the quadratic 5 − 4x − x². The quadratic has vertex at x = −b/(2a) = 4/(−2) = −2. At x = −2: 5 − 4(−2) − (−2)² = 5 + 8 − 4 = 9. The maximum value of f is logₖ(9) = 2, so k² = 9, and since k > 1, k = 3.

(b) Hence, find ∫ f(x) dx. [3]
questions.solution: (a) Expand the numerator and divide each term by x: (x − 1)²/x = (x² − 2x + 1)/x = x − 2 + 1/x, as required. (b) Therefore ∫f(x) dx = ∫(x − 2 + 1/x) dx = x²/2 − 2x + ln|x| + C.

2. [Maximum mark: 6]

The points A and B lie on a circle, with centre O and radius 19.5 cm, such that BÔA = 210°.

A piece of paper is cut into the shape of the sector BOA.

A hollow cone with no base is constructed from the sector by joining the points A and B. The sector forms the curved surface of the cone.

This is shown in the following diagrams.

[Diagrams: On the left, sector BOA is the major sector of a circle. Its centre is O; straight radii OA and OB are each labelled 19.5 cm; the reflex central angle BÔA is labelled 210°; and the major arc runs from B around the left side of the circle to A. On the right, the sector has been formed into a hollow cone with vertex O. The two radii become coincident slant edges of length 19.5 cm, and the joined point on the circular rim is labelled A, B. The visible front half of the circular rim is solid and the hidden rear half is dashed.]

Find

(a) the area of the sector BOA; [3]

(b) the radius of the cone. [3]
questions.solution: (a) The sector angle is 210° = 7π/6 radians. Its area is ½r²θ = ½(19.5)²(7π/6) = 3549π/16 = 696.844… cm², so the area is 697 cm² to three significant figures. (b) When the sector is formed into the cone, its arc becomes the base circumference. The arc length is 19.5(7π/6) = 91π/4 cm. If R is the cone's radius, 2πR = 91π/4, so R = 91/8 = 11.375 cm = 11.4 cm to three significant figures.

At the start of 2022, the population was 6.78 × 10⁶.

5. [Maximum mark: 8]

In a study, measurements for arm span, A cm, and foot length, F cm, are taken from a large group of adults.

For this group, the regression line of F on A is found to be F = 0.335A − 32.6, and the regression line of A on F is found to be A = 2.89F + 99.3. Each regression line passes through the mean point.

(a) By using an appropriate regression line, find an estimate of the arm span for an adult with a foot length of 19.8 cm. [2]

(b) For this group of adults, find the mean arm span and the mean foot length. [3]

The heights, H cm, of adults in the group can be modelled by a normal distribution with mean 163 cm and standard deviation σ cm.

It is found that 88% of the group have a height between 153 cm and 173 cm.

(c) Find the value of σ. [3]
questions.solution: (a) Arm span is the response variable, so use the regression of A on F: A = 2.89(19.8) + 99.3 = 156.522 cm, giving 157 cm to three significant figures. (b) Both regression lines pass through (Ā, F̄), so solve F̄ = 0.335Ā − 32.6 and Ā = 2.89F̄ + 99.3 simultaneously. This gives F̄ = 20.8948… cm and Ā = 159.686… cm. Thus the mean foot length is 20.9 cm and the mean arm span is 160 cm. (c) The interval from 153 to 173 is symmetric about the mean 163. Since its probability is 0.88, each tail has probability 0.06, so P(H < 173) = 0.94. Therefore (173 − 163)/σ = Φ⁻¹(0.94) = 1.55477…, and σ = 10/1.55477… = 6.43180… cm ≈ 6.43 cm.

6. [Maximum mark: 6]

Consider the function h(x) = 15 cos(πx/50) + 15, where 0 ≤ x ≤ 50.

The tangent, Tₖ, to the curve y = h(x) at the point (k, h(k)) is shown on the following diagram.

[Diagram: Coordinate axes are labelled x and y, with the origin labelled 0, y = 30 marked on the vertical axis and x = 50 marked on the horizontal axis. The curve labelled y = h(x) starts at (0, 30) with a horizontal tangent, decreases in a cosine-shaped arc, and ends at (50, 0) with a horizontal tangent. A point on the upper-left portion of the curve is marked and labelled (k, h(k)). The descending straight tangent through this point is labelled Tₖ; it crosses the positive x-axis to the right of 50.]

(a) Find the gradient of Tₖ in terms of k. [3]

Consider the case where the angle between Tₖ and the x-axis is π/8 radians.

(b) Find the possible values of k. [3]
questions.solution: (a) Differentiating h(x) gives h′(x) = 15[−sin(πx/50)](π/50) = −(3π/10)sin(πx/50). Hence the gradient of Tₖ is −(3π/10)sin(πk/50). (b) On 0 ≤ k ≤ 50 the tangent gradient is non-positive. An acute angle π/8 with the x-axis therefore corresponds to gradient −tan(π/8). Thus −(3π/10)sin(πk/50) = −tan(π/8), or sin(πk/50) = 10tan(π/8)/(3π) = 0.439494…. Solving on 0 ≤ k ≤ 50 gives k = 7.24211… or k = 42.7578…, so k = 7.24 or 42.8 to three significant figures.

questions.summary: Build a discrete score distribution from two dice, calculate its expectation, and find a five-round prize probability.
questions.accessibleText:
7. [Maximum mark: 14]

Lynn is playing a game with two unbiased six-sided dice, each with faces marked with the integers from 1 to 6.

In each round, she throws both dice once. The outcomes can be displayed in the following sample space diagram, which has been partially completed:

[Sample space diagram: A 6 by 6 interior grid has Die 2 as the column heading and Die 1 as the row heading. The six columns are labelled 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 from left to right, and the six rows are labelled 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 from top to bottom. Three ordered outcomes are printed: 2,2 in row 2, column 2; 3,4 in row 3, column 4; and 5,3 in row 5, column 3. Every other interior cell is blank.]

Lynn scores points according to the following rules.

• If the two dice show the same score, she scores 10 points.

• If the two dice show scores which have a difference of one, for example the scores 4 and 5 in any order, she scores 5 points.

• Otherwise, she scores 0 points.

(a) Show that the probability that Lynn scores 5 points in one round is 5/18. [2]

(b) Find the probability that Lynn scores no points in one round. [2]

The random variable X represents the number of points Lynn scores in one round.

(c) Find E(X). [4]

(d) Hence, estimate the total number of points that Lynn scores if she plays 90 rounds. [2]

A prize is awarded to any player who scores more than 40 points in total.

Lynn plays exactly five rounds.

(e) Find the probability that Lynn wins a prize. [4]
questions.solution: (a) A difference of one occurs for (1,2), (2,1), (2,3), (3,2), (3,4), (4,3), (4,5), (5,4), (5,6) and (6,5): 10 of the 36 equally likely outcomes. Thus P(X = 5) = 10/36 = 5/18. (b) There are 6 equal-score outcomes, so P(X = 10) = 6/36 = 1/6. Therefore P(X = 0) = 1 − 5/18 − 1/6 = 5/9. (c) E(X) = 0(5/9) + 5(5/18) + 10(1/6) = 25/18 + 30/18 = 55/18 = 3.05555… points. (d) Over 90 rounds, the expected total is 90(55/18) = 275 points. (e) More than 40 points in five rounds can occur only as five 10-point scores, or as four 10-point scores and one 5-point score. Hence P(win) = (1/6)⁵ + C(5,1)(1/6)⁴(5/18) = 7/5832 = 0.00120027… ≈ 0.00120.

Rectangular playing cards are stacked in the shape of a pyramid with n rows, where n ≥ 1.

Some cards are placed horizontally and some cards are stacked at an angle of 60° to the horizontal.

The following diagrams represent pyramid stacks for n = 1, n = 2 and n = 3.

[Diagrams: For n = 1, two inclined cards lean together to form one inverted-V support, with no horizontal card. For n = 2, two inverted-V supports stand in the bottom row, one horizontal card bridges their apexes, and one inverted-V support stands on that card: six inclined cards and one horizontal card in total. For n = 3, three inverted-V supports form the bottom row and two horizontal cards bridge adjacent apexes; two inverted-V supports form the second row and one horizontal card bridges their apexes; one inverted-V support forms the top row: twelve inclined cards and three horizontal cards in total. The visible left face of each inverted-V support is shaded grey.]

Let tₙ represent the number of cards used to create a pyramid stack with n rows.

(a) Write down t₃. [1]

(b) Find t₄. [2]

(c) Show that tₙ = n(3n + 1)/2. [3]

There are 52 cards in a full pack of playing cards.

(d) A complete pyramid stack is created using playing cards taken from 14 full packs. Find the maximum number of rows in this stack. [3]

(e) A complete pyramid stack is created using playing cards taken from full packs with no cards left over. Find the minimum number of rows in this stack. [2]

The long edge of each playing card measures 88 mm as illustrated in the following diagram.

[Diagram: Two inclined rectangular cards lean together as one inverted-V support. The long sloping edge of the right-hand card is labelled 88 mm; the visible left face is shaded grey.]

(f) Find the minimum number of cards needed to create a complete pyramid stack with a vertical height of more than 2 metres. The thickness of the cards may be ignored. [5]
questions.solution: (a) The n = 3 diagram contains 12 inclined cards and 3 horizontal cards, so t₃ = 15. (b) A fourth row adds 2(4) = 8 inclined cards and 3 horizontal cards, so t₄ = 15 + 11 = 26. (c) Row r contributes 2r inclined cards and r − 1 horizontal cards, for 3r − 1 cards. Therefore tₙ = Σᵣ₌₁ⁿ(3r − 1) = 3n(n + 1)/2 − n = n(3n + 1)/2, as required. (d) Fourteen packs contain 14(52) = 728 cards. Solve n(3n + 1)/2 ≤ 728. The positive boundary is n = (−1 + √17473)/6 = 21.8642…. Also t₂₁ = 672 and t₂₂ = 737, so the maximum is 21 rows. (e) The stack must use a positive multiple of 52 cards. Checking tₙ = n(3n + 1)/2 in increasing order, no value for 1 ≤ n ≤ 12 is divisible by 52, while t₁₃ = 13(40)/2 = 260 = 5(52). Thus the minimum is 13 rows. (f) The vertical height contributed by each row is 88sin60° = 44√3 = 76.2102… mm. More than 2 m means n(44√3) > 2000, so n > 26.2431… and the minimum is n = 27 rows. The number of cards is t₂₇ = 27(82)/2 = 1107.

questions.summary: Analyse self-inverse rational functions, minimize distance to the origin, and sketch a reciprocal rational graph with its asymptotes and discontinuity.
questions.accessibleText:
9. [Maximum mark: 15]

Consider the function f(x) = (2 − 2x)/(x + 2), where x ∈ ℝ, x ≠ −2.

(a) Show that f⁻¹(x) = f(x). [3]

The point P(k, (2 − 2k)/(k + 2)) is the point on the graph of y = f(x) that is closest to the origin (0, 0).

(b) (i) Find the value of k.

(ii) Hence, write down the coordinates of P. [4]

Consider the function g(x) = (2 − 3x)/(cx + d), where x ∈ ℝ, x ≠ −d/c, and c, d ≠ 0.

The graph of y = g(x) has a vertical asymptote and a horizontal asymptote.

(c) In terms of c and d, write down the equation of

(i) the vertical asymptote;

(ii) the horizontal asymptote. [2]

It is given that g⁻¹(x) = g(x).

(d) Find the value of d. [2]

Consider the case where c = 1.

(e) Sketch the graph of y = 1/g(x), showing the values of any intercepts with the axes and including any asymptotes, labelled with their equations. [4]
questions.solution: (a) Let y = (2 − 2x)/(x + 2). Then yx + 2y = 2 − 2x, so x(y + 2) = 2 − 2y and x = (2 − 2y)/(y + 2) = f(y). Interchanging x and y therefore gives f⁻¹(x) = f(x). (b)(i) The graph is symmetric in y = x because f is its own inverse. Its two intersections with y = x satisfy k = (2 − 2k)/(k + 2), so k² + 4k − 2 = 0 and k = −2 ± √6. The nearer intersection to the origin is k = −2 + √6 = 0.449489…; the other has k = −4.44948…. Hence k = 0.449 to three significant figures. (ii) At this closest point f(k) = k, so P = (√6 − 2, √6 − 2), or (0.449, 0.449) to three significant figures. (c)(i) The denominator is zero when cx + d = 0, so the vertical asymptote is x = −d/c. (ii) The ratio of the leading coefficients is −3/c, so the horizontal asymptote is y = −3/c. (d) Solving y = (2 − 3x)/(cx + d) for x gives g⁻¹(y) = (2 − dy)/(cy + 3). For this to equal g(y) = (2 − 3y)/(cy + d), comparison of the constant terms after cross-multiplication gives 2d = 6, hence d = 3. (e) With c = 1 and d = 3, 1/g(x) = (x + 3)/(2 − 3x), subject to the original domain restriction x ≠ −3. The vertical asymptote is x = 2/3 and the horizontal asymptote is y = −1/3. The y-intercept is (0, 3/2). The simplified expression would be zero at x = −3, but that value is excluded, so show an open point discontinuity at (−3, 0), not an included x-intercept. Draw two decreasing rational branches: for x < 2/3 the branch approaches y = −1/3 from above as x → −∞, has the open point at (−3, 0), passes through (0, 3/2), and tends to +∞ as x → (2/3)⁻; for x > 2/3 the branch tends to −∞ as x → (2/3)⁺ and approaches y = −1/3 from below as x → ∞.

A particle P moves in a straight line. The velocity v m s⁻¹ of P, at time t seconds is given by v(t) = e^(−sin t) cos(2t), for 0 ≤ t ≤ 5.

(a) Find the maximum speed of P. [2]

(b) Find the total distance travelled by P. [2]

(c) Find the acceleration when P changes direction for the second time. [3]
questions.solution: (a) Maximum speed occurs when |v| is greatest. At t = 4.71238…, v = −2.71828… = −e, so the maximum speed is e ≈ 2.72 m s⁻¹. (b) Total distance = ∫₀⁵|v(t)| dt = 3.84591… ≈ 3.85 m. Ball 1 is dropped from a height of 10 metres.

(a) Find the maximum height of Ball 1 after the 5th bounce. [3]

(b) Find the total distance travelled by Ball 1 immediately before the 5th bounce. [3]

(c) A ball is dropped from a height of x metres. Show that d = 5x metres. [3]

(d) Write down the value of d₁. [1]

It is given that d₁, d₂, d₃, ... form an arithmetic sequence.

(e) Determine which tennis ball is the first ball to travel less than 25 metres. [4]
questions.solution: (a) Geometric sequence with r=2/3: height after 5th bounce = 10×(2/3)^5 = 320/243 = 1.31687…≈1.32 m. (b) Total distance = 10 + 2×10×(2/3) + 2×10×(2/3)² + 2×10×(2/3)³ + 2×10×(2/3)^4 = 10 + 2×10×(2/3)(1−(2/3)^4)/(1−2/3) = 42.0987…≈42.1 m. (c) Using sum to infinity for vertical travel after first drop: d = x + 2×x×(2/3)/(1−2/3) = x + 2x×(2/3)×3 = x + 4x = 5x. (d) d₁ = 5×10 = 50 m. (e) d₂ = 5×9.56 = 47.8. Since x > 7, all cancelled factors and denominators are non-zero, so [x/((x − 1)(x − 7))]·[((x − 1)(x + 1))/(x + 1)] = x/(x − 7), as required. f(x) = −x² + 4x + p and

g(x) = x² + qx − 1,

where p and q are non-zero constants.

The graph of y = f(x) has a vertex at A and the graph of y = g(x) has a vertex at B.

Points A and B both lie on the line y = 2x − 1.

(a) Show that p = −1. [3]

(b) Find the value of q. [5]
questions.solution: Complete the square for f: f(x) = −(x − 2)² + 4 + p, so A = (2, 4 + p). Since A lies on y = 2x − 1, its y-coordinate is 2(2) − 1 = 3. Thus 4 + p = 3 and (a) p = −1. For g, complete the square: g(x) = (x + q/2)² − q²/4 − 1, so B = (−q/2, −q²/4 − 1). The line has y = 2(−q/2) − 1 = −q − 1 at this x-coordinate. Hence −q²/4 − 1 = −q − 1, so q² = 4q and q(q − 4) = 0. Since q is non-zero, (b) q = 4.
questions.solutionStatus: Independent worked solutions — checked against the official IB markscheme

questions.summary: Work with linear functions, inverses and composition, then relate the graphs of a function and its inverse.
questions.accessibleText:
7. [Maximum mark: 14]

Consider the function f(x) = 2x + 3 where x ∈ ℝ.

(a) Find
    (i) f(2);
    (ii) f⁻¹(x). [3]

The following diagram shows part of the graph of a linear function h.

The graph has x-intercept 2 and y-intercept −1.

[Diagram: Coordinate axes labelled x and y from −3 to 3. The increasing straight line y = h(x) crosses the y-axis at (0, −1) and the x-axis at (2, 0); it also passes through points such as (−2, −2).]

(b) Write down an expression for h(x). [2]

(c) Solve the equation h⁻¹(x) = −2. [2]

Consider the function g(x) = mx + c, where x ∈ ℝ and m, c ∈ ℚ.

(d) Given that h(x) = (f⁻¹ ∘ g)(x), find the value of m and the value of c. [4]

A function k exists such that h(k(x)) = x.

(e) Find an expression for k(x). [2]

(f) State the single transformation that maps the graph of y = k(x) onto the graph of y = h(x). [1]
questions.solution: (a)(i) f(2) = 2(2) + 3 = 7. (a)(ii) Let y = 2x + 3, interchange x and y, and solve: x = 2y + 3, so f⁻¹(x) = (x − 3)/2. (b) The slope of h through (0, −1) and (2, 0) is [0 − (−1)]/(2 − 0) = 1/2, hence h(x) = x/2 − 1. (c) Since h⁻¹(x) = 2x + 2, solve 2x + 2 = −2 to get x = −2. (d) (f⁻¹ ∘ g)(x) = f⁻¹(mx + c) = (mx + c − 3)/2. Equating this with h(x) = x/2 − 1 gives m = 1 and (c − 3)/2 = −1, so c = 1. (e) The identity h(k(x)) = x means k = h⁻¹, so k(x) = 2x + 2. (f) The graphs of a function and its inverse are reflections of one another in the line y = x. Therefore the required transformation is reflection in the line y = x.

8. [Maximum mark: 14]

The function f has a derivative given by f′(x) = 3x² + 12x − 15.

The graph of y = f(x) has horizontal tangents at the points where x = a and x = b, a < b.

(a) Find the value of a and the value of b. [3]

The following diagram shows three intervals along the x-axis defined by a and b. The sign of the first derivative of f is shown in each interval.

[Sign diagram for f′: positive for x < a, zero at a, negative for a < x < b, zero at b, and positive for x > b.]

(b) State, with a reason, whether there is a local maximum point or a local minimum point on the graph of y = f(x) at x = a. [2]

The second derivative f″(x) is zero at x = c.

(c) Find the value of c. [3]

The following diagram shows two intervals along the x-axis defined by c. The sign of the second derivative is shown in each interval.

[Sign diagram for f″: negative for x < c, zero at c, and positive for x > c.]

(d) State, with a reason, whether there is a point of inflexion on the graph of y = f(x) at x = c. [2]

(e) Given that f(−2) = 36, find f(x). [4]
questions.solution: (a) Horizontal tangents occur where f′(x) = 0. Factor 3x² + 12x − 15 = 3(x² + 4x − 5) = 3(x + 5)(x − 1). Thus a = −5 and b = 1. (b) At x = a, f′ changes from positive to negative, so f changes from increasing to decreasing; therefore f has a local maximum there. (c) f″(x) = 6x + 12. Setting this equal to zero gives c = −2. (d) Yes. The sign diagram shows f″ changing from negative to positive at c, so the concavity of f changes and there is a point of inflexion at x = c. (e) Integrating, f(x) = x³ + 6x² − 15x + C. Using f(−2) = 36 gives −8 + 24 + 30 + C = 36, so C = −10. Hence f(x) = x³ + 6x² − 15x − 10.

questions.summary: Derive the tangent form of the double-angle identity, solve a trigonometric equation, and obtain the exact value of tan 22.5°.

9. [Maximum mark: 15]

(a) Show that 2tan θ/(1 + tan²θ) can be expressed as sin 2θ. [3]

(b) Hence, solve the equation 2tan θ/(1 + tan²θ) = 1/2 for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 180°. [5]

Let x = tan(22 1/2°).

(c) Use the result from part (a) to show that x² − 2√2x + 1 = 0. [4]

(d) Hence, find the exact value of tan(22 1/2°). [3]
questions.solution: (a) Substitute tan θ = sin θ/cos θ: [2(sin θ/cos θ)]/[1 + sin²θ/cos²θ] = [2sin θ cos θ]/[cos²θ + sin²θ] = 2sin θ cos θ = sin 2θ. (b) The equation becomes sin 2θ = 1/2. Since 0° ≤ 2θ ≤ 360°, 2θ = 30° or 150°, so θ = 15° or 75°. (c) With x = tan 22.5°, part (a) gives 2x/(1 + x²) = sin 45° = √2/2. Therefore 4x = √2(1 + x²), so x² − 2√2x + 1 = 0, as required. (d) The quadratic formula gives x = [2√2 ± √(8 − 4)]/2 = √2 ± 1. Since 0° < 22.5° < 45°, 0 < tan 22.5° < 1, so the valid root is tan(22.5°) = √2 − 1.

2. [Maximum mark: 5]

The gradient of a curve is given by dy/dx = 4 cos x − sin x. The curve passes through the point (π, 3). Find the equation of the curve.
questions.solution: Integrating the gradient gives y = ∫(4 cos x − sin x) dx = 4 sin x + cos x + C. The point (π, 3) lies on the curve, so 3 = 4 sin π + cos π + C = 0 − 1 + C. Thus C = 4, and the equation of the curve is y = 4 sin x + cos x + 4.

3. [Maximum mark: 5]

The 7th term of an arithmetic sequence is 6.

The sum of the 6th term and the 12th term is 24.

Find the first term and the common difference.
questions.solution: Let the first term be u₁ and the common difference be d. Since uₙ = u₁ + (n − 1)d, the seventh-term condition gives u₁ + 6d = 6. Also, u₆ + u₁₂ = (u₁ + 5d) + (u₁ + 11d) = 24, so 2u₁ + 16d = 24, or u₁ + 8d = 12. Subtracting u₁ + 6d = 6 gives 2d = 6, hence d = 3. Then u₁ + 18 = 6, so u₁ = −12. The first term is −12 and the common difference is 3.

4. [Maximum mark: 6]

Events A and B are such that P(A) = 1/2, P(B) = 1/3 and P(A | B) = 1/4.

(a) Find the probability that both events A and B occur. [2]

(b) Find P(A | B′). [4]
questions.solution:
(a) By the definition of conditional probability, P(A ∩ B) = P(A | B)P(B) = (1/4)(1/3) = 1/12.

(b) P(B′) = 1 − 1/3 = 2/3. Also, P(A ∩ B′) = P(A) − P(A ∩ B) = 1/2 − 1/12 = 5/12. Therefore P(A | B′) = P(A ∩ B′)/P(B′) = (5/12)/(2/3) = (5/12)(3/2) = 5/8.

5. [Maximum mark: 8]

The following diagram shows the graph of y = (Ax + B)/(x − 4), where x ∈ ℝ, x ≠ 4 and A, B ∈ ℤ.

The graph passes through the points P(−10, 1) and Q(3, −12).

[Coordinate diagram: a reciprocal-type graph has vertical asymptote x = 4 and horizontal asymptote y = 2. Its left branch passes through P(−10, 1), crosses the x-axis to the left of the y-axis, passes below the y-axis and through Q(3, −12), then tends downward as x approaches 4 from the left. Its right branch tends upward as x approaches 4 from the right and approaches y = 2 from above as x increases.]

(a) Determine the value of A and the value of B. [3]

(b) Describe a sequence of transformations that would map the graph of y = 1/x onto the graph of y = (Ax + B)/(x − 4). [5]
questions.solution:
(a) Substituting P(−10, 1) into y = (Ax + B)/(x − 4) gives 1 = (−10A + B)/(−14), so −10A + B = −14. Substituting Q(3, −12) gives −12 = (3A + B)/(−1), so 3A + B = 12. Subtracting the first equation from the second gives 13A = 26, hence A = 2. Then 3(2) + B = 12, so B = 6.

(b) With A = 2 and B = 6, y = (2x + 6)/(x − 4) = 2 + 14/(x − 4). Starting from y = 1/x: apply a vertical stretch by scale factor 14; translate 4 units to the right; then translate 2 units upwards. The horizontal translation may be performed before or after the vertical stretch, but the vertical stretch must precede the upward translation.

Solve the equation 3 log₈(10x) − log₄ x = 1 for x > 0.
questions.solution: Convert all logarithms to base 2. Since log₈(10x) = log₂(10x)/3 and log₄x = log₂x/2, the equation becomes log₂(10x) − (1/2)log₂x = 1. Using logarithm laws, log₂(10x) − log₂(√x) = log₂(10√x) = 1. Therefore 10√x = 2, so √x = 1/5 and x = 1/25, which satisfies x > 0.

questions.summary: Apply the cosine rule to two triangles, solve a resulting quadratic under side-length constraints, and calculate an exact area.
questions.accessibleText:
7. [Maximum mark: 14]

Consider a triangle PQR where PR = 3, QR = 2 and P̂RQ = 60°.

[Diagram not to scale: triangle PQR has P at the lower left, R at the lower right and Q above them. The horizontal side PR is labelled 3, side QR is labelled 2, and the interior angle at R is labelled 60°.]

(a) Find PQ. [3]

Now consider a general triangle ABC where AC = x + 2, BC = 3x − 1 and AĈB = 60°.

[Diagram: triangle ABC has A at the lower left, C at the lower right and B above them. The horizontal side AC is labelled x + 2, side BC is labelled 3x − 1, and the interior angle at C is labelled 60°.]

(b) Show that AB = √(7x² − 7x + 7). [5]

(c) Given that AB = 7,

(i) find the value of x;

(ii) find the area of triangle ABC. [6]
questions.solution:
(a) By the cosine rule, PQ² = PR² + QR² − 2(PR)(QR)cos 60° = 3² + 2² − 2(3)(2)(1/2) = 9 + 4 − 6 = 7. Therefore PQ = √7.

(b) Applying the cosine rule at C, AB² = (x + 2)² + (3x − 1)² − 2(x + 2)(3x − 1)cos 60°. Since cos 60° = 1/2, AB² = (x + 2)² + (3x − 1)² − (x + 2)(3x − 1). Expanding gives AB² = (x² + 4x + 4) + (9x² − 6x + 1) − (3x² + 5x − 2) = 7x² − 7x + 7. As AB is a length, AB = √(7x² − 7x + 7), as required.

(c)(i) Set √(7x² − 7x + 7) = 7. Squaring gives 7x² − 7x + 7 = 49, so x² − x − 6 = 0. Hence (x − 3)(x + 2) = 0, giving x = 3 or x = −2. But AC = x + 2 and BC = 3x − 1 must be positive; x = −2 is invalid. Therefore x = 3.

(c)(ii) When x = 3, AC = 5 and BC = 8. Thus area = (1/2)(AC)(BC)sin 60° = (1/2)(5)(8)(√3/2) = 10√3.
questions.solutionStatus: Independent worked solutions — checked against the official IB markscheme

questions.summary: Analyze a quadratic using its discriminant and vertex, derive a normal line, and integrate the area between the line and curve.

8. [Maximum mark: 15]

Consider the function defined by f(x) = (1/2)x² + kx + 13, where x ∈ ℝ and k ∈ ℤ⁺.

(a) Given that the equation f(x) = 0 has no real roots, show that the greatest possible value of k is 5. [2]

For the remainder of this question, consider the case k = 5.

(b) (i) Write down the equation of the axis of symmetry of the graph of f.

(ii) Hence, or otherwise, determine the coordinates of the minimum point on the graph of f. [3]

The following diagram shows the graph of f and a line L which is normal to the curve at x = −3. The shaded area shown is bounded by the curve, the line L and the y-axis.

[Coordinate diagram: an upward-opening parabola has its minimum above the x-axis and to the left of the y-axis. A descending line L meets the curve at x = −3 and crosses the y-axis at 1. The region between the parabola and L from their meeting point at x = −3 to the y-axis x = 0 is shaded.]

(c) Show that the equation of L is given by y = −(1/2)x + 1. [5]

(d) Hence, find the shaded area. [5]
questions.solution:
(a) For f(x) = (1/2)x² + kx + 13, the discriminant is Δ = k² − 4(1/2)(13) = k² − 26. No real roots requires Δ < 0, so k² < 26. Since k is a positive integer, k ≤ 5; therefore the greatest possible value is 5.

(b)(i) With k = 5, the axis of symmetry is x = −b/(2a) = −5/[2(1/2)] = −5.

(b)(ii) f(−5) = (1/2)(25) + 5(−5) + 13 = 25/2 − 25 + 13 = 1/2. Hence the minimum point is (−5, 1/2).

(c) At x = −3, f(−3) = (1/2)(9) − 15 + 13 = 5/2, so the point is (−3, 5/2). Also f′(x) = x + 5, giving tangent gradient f′(−3) = 2. The normal gradient is the negative reciprocal, −1/2. Therefore y − 5/2 = −(1/2)(x + 3), which simplifies to y = −(1/2)x + 1.

(d) On −3 ≤ x ≤ 0, the parabola lies above L. The shaded area is ∫ from −3 to 0 of [(1/2)x² + 5x + 13 − (−(1/2)x + 1)] dx = ∫ from −3 to 0 of [(1/2)x² + (11/2)x + 12] dx. An antiderivative is x³/6 + 11x²/4 + 12x. Therefore the area is [x³/6 + 11x²/4 + 12x] from −3 to 0 = 0 − [−27/6 + 99/4 − 36] = 63/4 square units.
questions.solutionStatus: Independent worked solutions — checked against the official IB markscheme

9. [Maximum mark: 16]

The function f is defined by f(x) = (5eˣ − e²ˣ)/(eˣ + 1). The following diagram shows part of the graph of f. The graph intersects the y-axis at point P and intersects the x-axis at point R.

Point Q is a local maximum point with coordinates (q, 7 − 2√6).

[Coordinate diagram: the curve approaches the x-axis from above on the far left, rises through P on the y-axis to the nearby local maximum Q just to the right of the y-axis, then falls, crosses the positive x-axis at R, and continues downward.]

(a) (i) Find the coordinates of point P.

(ii) Find the coordinates of point R. [6]

(b) State the range of f. [1]

(c) Show that f′(x) = (−e³ˣ − 2e²ˣ + 5eˣ)/(eˣ + 1)². [3]

(d) Hence, show that q = ln(√6 − 1). [6]
questions.solution:
(a)(i) At x = 0, f(0) = (5e⁰ − e⁰)/(e⁰ + 1) = (5 − 1)/2 = 2. Hence P = (0, 2).

(a)(ii) At an x-intercept, 5eˣ − e²ˣ = 0. Factorizing gives eˣ(5 − eˣ) = 0. Since eˣ > 0, eˣ = 5, so x = ln 5. Hence R = (ln 5, 0).

(b) The local maximum Q is the global maximum shown by the function's end behaviour, and its y-coordinate is 7 − 2√6. Therefore the range is f(x) ≤ 7 − 2√6, equivalently (−∞, 7 − 2√6].

(c) Let u = 5eˣ − e²ˣ and v = eˣ + 1. Then u′ = 5eˣ − 2e²ˣ and v′ = eˣ. By the quotient rule, f′(x) = [(eˣ + 1)(5eˣ − 2e²ˣ) − eˣ(5eˣ − e²ˣ)]/(eˣ + 1)². Expanding the numerator gives 5e²ˣ + 5eˣ − 2e³ˣ − 2e²ˣ − 5e²ˣ + e³ˣ = −e³ˣ − 2e²ˣ + 5eˣ. Thus f′(x) = (−e³ˣ − 2e²ˣ + 5eˣ)/(eˣ + 1)², as required.

(d) At Q, f′(q) = 0. The denominator is positive, so −e^(3q) − 2e^(2q) + 5e^q = 0. Dividing by e^q > 0 gives −e^(2q) − 2e^q + 5 = 0, or (e^q)² + 2e^q − 5 = 0. Solving this quadratic gives e^q = −1 ± √6. Since e^q > 0, e^q = √6 − 1. Taking natural logarithms yields q = ln(√6 − 1).

The following diagram shows a regular pentagon inscribed in a circle with centre O and radius r cm.

The angle AÔB is θ, where θ is measured in radians.

[Diagram not to scale: A regular pentagon is inscribed in a circle with centre O. Adjacent vertices A and B lie near the top of the circle. Radii OA and OB are drawn; OA is labelled r and the central angle AÔB is labelled θ. The minor arc AB is labelled 12. The five circular segments between the sides of the pentagon and the circumference are shaded.]

(a) Find

(a) Find P(Z < 1.7). [1]

It is known that P(a < Z < 1.7) = 0.7865, correct to four significant figures.

(b) Sketch this information on the following diagram. [1]

3. [Maximum mark: 7]

Data was collected on two variables, x and y, from eight members of a population. The data is shown in the table below.

[Table: x: 3.8, 6.3, 2.5, 2.4, 8.9, 10.7, 6.7, 10.3. Corresponding y: 11.8, 9.7, 6.1, 4.1, p, 23.3, 13.7, 24.5.]

(a) Find x̄. [2]

The regression line of y on x for this data is y = 0.014375 + 2.1625x.

(b) Find

(i) ȳ;

(ii) the value of p. [4]

(c) Hence, find Pearson’s product-moment correlation coefficient, r. [1]
questions.solution: (a) x̄ = (3.8 + 6.3 + 2.5 + 2.4 + 8.9 + 10.7 + 6.7 + 10.3)/8 = 51.6/8 = 6.45. (b)(i) A least-squares regression line passes through (x̄, ȳ), so ȳ = 0.014375 + 2.1625(6.45) = 13.9625 ≈ 14.0. (ii) Therefore Σy = 8(13.9625) = 111.7. The seven known y-values sum to 93.2, hence p = 111.7 − 93.2 = 18.5. (c) Using the completed paired data, r = Σ((x − x̄)(y − ȳ))/√(Σ(x − x̄)² Σ(y − ȳ)²) = 0.953958… ≈ 0.954. All results agree with the official markscheme.

Consider the function g(x) = a cos(bx) − 3, where x ∈ ℝ and a, b ∈ ℝ.

The following diagram shows part of the graph of g.

[Diagram: Coordinate axes are labelled x and y. A smooth increasing half-wave begins at the local minimum (0, −8), rises through the x-axis, and ends at the local maximum (16, 2).]

The graph of g has a local minimum at (0, −8) and a local maximum at (16, 2).

(i) Find the smallest positive value of q.

(c) With b = π/16, shifting the sine curve right by 8 gives sin((π/16)(x − 8)); at x = 0 this equals −1 and at x = 16 it equals 1. questions.accessibleText:
6. [Maximum mark: 7]

Two machines are used in a factory to manufacture semiconductors. Machine A manufactures defective semiconductors 10% of the time, while machine B manufactures defective semiconductors 5% of the time.

A randomly selected machine manufactures ten semiconductors.

Both machines are equally likely to be selected.

(a) Find the probability that exactly two semiconductors are defective. [4]

(b) Given that exactly two semiconductors are defective, find the probability that they were manufactured by machine A. [3]
questions.solution: Let D be the event that exactly two of the ten semiconductors are defective. For machine A, P(D|A) = C(10,2)(0.10)²(0.90)⁸ = 0.193710…. For machine B, P(D|B) = C(10,2)(0.05)²(0.95)⁸ = 0.0746348…. (a) Since each machine is selected with probability 0.5, P(D) = 0.5P(D|A) + 0.5P(D|B) = 0.134172… ≈ 0.134. (b) By Bayes’ theorem, P(A|D) = 0.5P(D|A)/P(D) = 0.0968551…/0.134172… = 0.721870… ≈ 0.722. Both answers agree with the official markscheme.
questions.solutionStatus: Independent worked solutions — checked against the official IB markscheme

questions.summary: Analyse a rational function’s asymptotes and derivative, then minimize the distance from its left branch to a fixed point.
questions.accessibleText:
7. [Maximum mark: 13]

Consider the function f(x) = (3x + 1)/(2x − 4) where x ≠ 2.

(a) Write down the equation of

(i) the vertical asymptote of the graph of f;

(ii) the horizontal asymptote of the graph of f. [2]

(b) Find f′(x). [4]

(c) Hence, explain briefly why f is never increasing. [2]

The point P(x, f(x)) is on the graph of f such that x < 2.

Let d be the distance between the points P and Q(3, 5).

(d) Find an expression for d in terms of x. [2]

(e) Hence, find the coordinates of P such that d is a minimum. [3]
questions.solution: (a)(i) The denominator is zero at x = 2, so the vertical asymptote is x = 2. (ii) The ratio of leading coefficients is 3/2, so the horizontal asymptote is y = 3/2. (b) By the quotient rule, f′(x) = [3(2x − 4) − 2(3x + 1)]/(2x − 4)² = −14/(2x − 4)². (c) For every x ≠ 2, (2x − 4)² > 0, hence f′(x) < 0. Thus f is decreasing on each interval of its domain and is never increasing. (d) By the distance formula, d = √((x − 3)² + (((3x + 1)/(2x − 4)) − 5)²). (e) Minimize d² for x < 2. Solving d(d²)/dx = 0 numerically gives x = −0.305218…. Then f(x) = −0.0182945…. Therefore P = (−0.305, −0.0183) to three significant figures. This agrees with the official markscheme.
questions.solutionStatus: Independent worked solutions — checked against the official IB markscheme

questions.summary: Compare exponential and logistic frog-population models, including growth, parameter recovery, and the logistic inflection point.
questions.accessibleText:
8. [Maximum mark: 14]

A population of frogs, F, in a swamp after t months, can be modelled by the function

F(t) = 1850 × 1.105ᵗ where t ≥ 0.

(a) Find the population of frogs after one year. [2]

(b) After x complete months, the population will be at least 35 000 frogs. Find the value of x. [3]

The function F can be written in the form F(t) = 1850eᵏᵗ.

(c) Find the exact value of k. [2]

(d) Find the rate at which the population of frogs is growing after 15 months. [2]

A more realistic model describing the population of frogs, G, after t months is given by

G(t) = 35000/(1 + Ae^(−0.0998t)) where t ≥ 0.

(e) After 15 months, this model predicts a population of 6995 frogs. Find the value of A. [2]

(f) Find the value of t when the rate of population growth is the greatest. [2]

(g) By considering the graph of G or otherwise, state one reason why G(t) is a more appropriate long-term model than F(t). [1]
questions.solution: (a) F(12) = 1850(1.105)¹² = 6130.827…, giving 6130 frogs to three significant figures (6131 if rounded to the nearest whole frog). (b) Solve 1850(1.105)ˣ ≥ 35000. This gives x ≥ ln(35000/1850)/ln(1.105) = 29.4471…, so after 30 complete months the population is first at least 35 000; x = 30. (c) Since 1.105ᵗ = e^(t ln 1.105), k = ln(1.105) exactly. (d) F′(t) = 1850(1.105)ᵗ ln(1.105), so F′(15) = 825.911… ≈ 826 frogs per month. (e) 6995 = 35000/(1 + Ae^(−0.0998·15)), so A = (35000/6995 − 1)e^(0.0998·15) = 17.8890… ≈ 17.9. (f) Logistic growth is greatest at the inflection point, where Ae^(−0.0998t) = 1. Hence t = ln(A)/0.0998 = 28.8996… ≈ 28.9 months. (g) G has a carrying capacity of 35 000 and therefore accounts for limited resources, whereas F grows without bound. All numerical results and the long-term justification agree with the official markscheme.
questions.solutionStatus: Independent worked solutions — checked against the official IB markscheme

questions.summary: Integrate two velocity models to obtain separation, then find the catch-up time and the car’s travel distance.
questions.accessibleText:
9. [Maximum mark: 17]

An airplane lands on a runway 100 metres in front of a stationary car. At the instant the airplane lands, the car begins to travel in the same direction towards the airplane.

[Diagram not to scale: A car and an airplane face to the right on the same runway. The car is behind the airplane, an arrow above the car points right, and the initial gap from the front of the car to the back of the airplane is labelled 100 m.]

Let t represent the number of seconds after the airplane lands. For t ≥ 0, the velocities of the airplane and the car in m s⁻¹, can be modelled by the following equations:

v_air = 60e^(−0.1t)

v_car = 5t

(a) When the airplane lands, write down the speed of

(i) the airplane;

(ii) the car. [2]

(b) Find

(i) the value of t when the airplane and the car have the same speed;

(ii) the speed at this time. [3]

Let d(t) represent the distance, in metres, between the car and the back of the airplane after t seconds.

(c) If d(0) = 100, find d(t). [7]

(d) Hence, find how long it takes for the car to reach the back of the airplane. [2]

(e) Find the distance travelled by the car when it reaches the back of the airplane. [3]
questions.solution: (a)(i) v_air(0) = 60e⁰ = 60 m s⁻¹. (ii) v_car(0) = 5(0) = 0 m s⁻¹. (b)(i) Equal speeds satisfy 60e^(−0.1t) = 5t. Solving numerically gives t = 6.35564… ≈ 6.36 s. (ii) The common speed is 5t = 31.7782… ≈ 31.8 m s⁻¹. (c) Measured from the car’s initial position, the airplane’s position is 100 + ∫₀ᵗ60e^(−0.1u) du = 700 − 600e^(−0.1t), while the car’s position is ∫₀ᵗ5u du = (5/2)t². Therefore d(t) = 700 − 600e^(−0.1t) − (5/2)t². This gives d(0) = 100 as required. (d) Solve d(t) = 0 for t > 0: t = 15.0586… ≈ 15.1 s. (e) The car travels (5/2)(15.0586…)² = 566.904… ≈ 567 m. All answers agree with the official markscheme.
